Some LCP solutions are available in a unified system, where all elements of production fall under a single-vendor solution. For example, Grabyo Producer22 is a fully webbased LCP solution that requires no specific cloud architecture to be managed by the customer. Or Grass Valley AMPP23 is a SaaS platform capable of LCP that can run with its data plane in a customer-managed cloud architecture. Alternatively, LCP solutions can be composed of elements of multiple products from different vendors that the customer considers optimal (such as in the Fox Sports MLB PoC), in which case a customer or systems integrator needs to architect a solution on the cloud and provide for product-to-product media flow interfacing. Once in the cloud, network transport between virtual compute instances and other services can take the form of the same long-GOP codecs with reliable transport protocols as used in “ground-to-cloud” transport. Alternatively, to reduce in-cloud latency, lower-latency solutions such as the I-frame codec of network digital interface (NDI) high bandwidth24 or the uncompressed cloud transport of AWS cloud digital interface (CDI) 25 can be used. The NDI infrastructure provides a mechanism for the registration and discovery of flows between multiple virtual instances that can aid in solution deployment. CDI uses multiple flows to reliably transport uncompressed media with low latency within the cloud. Putting it All Together A final example of LCP is The Broken Arrow Skyrace,26 a unique style of extreme mountain running characterized by off-trail climbing on steep terrain with massive amounts of vertical gain and loss at altitude. The race is situated on a mountainside, where it is difficult to deploy traditional means of live video capture technology. Services like power and network access are literally miles away. LiveSports produced a 4.5-hr stream of race coverage, utilizing a robust cloud-based multicamera remote production workflow. LiveU LU800 multicamera field units, capable of supporting up to four camera inputs each, allowed high-quality, high-definition (up to 4Kp60) contributions encoded in HEVC and transported with LRT over 4G and 5G bonded cellular connections in a resilient manner. Additional creative options were opened up using the LU-Smart mobile app that enabled video contribution from mobile devices deployed along the route. Camera/runners used LU-smart on gimbal-mounted phones to chase the racers, bringing the audience into the action. LiveU sources were transmitted to LiveU’s Cloud Connect virtualized LRT decode software, installed in LiveSport’s AWS EC2 instances. These output NDI video sources to the cloud architecture, including Vizrt’s Vectar Plus software production system for functionality such as video switching, audio mixing, keying, media players, and streaming encoders. The LiveSport team
